# Vertical overlay: Construction

**Level:** NAICS 2022 sector 23 (parent vertical)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Commercial and institutional building general contractor.
**Primary system:** Project management and payment application system

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
General Services Administration / federal contracting agencies (FAR); Department of Defense (DFARS/CMMC) for defense construction contractors; OSHA (safety; no cyber rules)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**FAR 52.204-21 / CMMC Level 1 (escalating to NIST SP 800-171 R2 / CMMC Level 2 when CUI is handled)**, 48 CFR 52.204-21; 32 CFR Part 170. Construction has no sector-specific cyber regulation; the binding obligations most firms face come through federal contracts. The 15 FAR requirements are the minimum; firms handling CUI (e.g., controlled building plans for federal/defense facilities) must meet DFARS 7012/NIST SP 800-171 R2 and CMMC Level 2.
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.204-21

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Federal Contract Information (FCI); CUI incl. controlled building/facility drawings; Employee PII and payroll (certified payroll/Davis-Bacon); Bid and pricing data; Client facility security details
- **Critical systems:** Project management and BIM/CAD platforms; ERP/accounting and payroll; Building automation/BAS installed for clients; Telematics for heavy equipment; Video surveillance and access control installs
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Business email compromise redirecting progress payments
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** AI estimating and bid assistant

## Notes
Not a CISA critical infrastructure sector; CIRCIA would reach construction firms only via another criterion (e.g., DFARS 7012 contractor). SEC cross-cutting note in n11.
